item.title: [LU-20531] cross-MDT close from ldlm_bl deadlocks the blocking-AST thread pool when the MDC import is not FULL
item.description:
On a DNE filesystem, an MDS can permanently deadlock its entire LDLM

blocking-AST (ldlm_bl) thread pool when a cross-MDT close is issued from lock

cancellation while the MDC import to the target MDT is not LUSTRE_IMP_FULL. All

lock cancellation on the affected MDS stops, the MDS begins evicting its own

internal client and then its regular clients, peer MDTs evict the affected MDS,

and the condition does not self-heal – only a reboot clears it.

 

Observed impact: on a 16-MDT production filesystem, two peer MDS entered this

state during failover of a third MDT. The filesystem was unusable for

approximately two hours and was recovered only by rebooting all MDS.
item.environment: 16-MDT DNE filesystem, ~535 TiB, Lustre 2.15, EL9 kernel (5.14.x). Triggered during failover/recovery of a single MDT.
item.summary: cross-MDT close from ldlm_bl deadlocks the blocking-AST thread pool when the MDC import is not FULL

status.description: The issue is open and ready for the assignee to start work on it.

comments.comment:
1. SUMMARY

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

An ldlm_bl thread, while performing a routine LRU lock cancellation, cancelled

a cross-MDT lock holding the MDS_INODELOCK_OPEN bit for a cached, deferred open

handle on an otherwise idle inode. Cancelling that lock pruned the last cached

dentry, dropped the final inode reference, and flushing the deferred open handle

to the MDT that owns the inode required a synchronous MDS_CLOSE RPC.

 

MDT-A's MDC import to MDT-B was not LUSTRE_IMP_FULL (MDT-B was in recovery), so

the close was delayed indefinitely by ptlrpc_import_delay_req() – while holding

the single close modify-RPC slot. Every subsequent ldlm_bl thread that reached a

close then blocked in obd_get_mod_rpc_slot() waiting for that one slot. Once the

pool was drained, MDT-A could no longer process any lock cancellation, including

the blocking ASTs its own server needed answered in order to grant conflicting

locks, so it began evicting its own internal client and then its regular

clients.

 

The state is unbreakable: the slot wait is TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE with

MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT and is woken only on modify-RPC completion – there is no

wakeup on import state change. When MDT-B's recovery subsequently aborted the

peer's lock replays and evicted it (setting the import invalid), the waiters

could never wake, because the RPC they were waiting behind could never complete.

 

 

2. CALL STACK EVIDENCE

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Ten ldlm_bl threads, all in state D, all with the identical stack:

 

    INFO: task ldlm_bl_01:24821 blocked for more than 122 seconds.

          (also ldlm_bl_02, _03, _05, _06, _10, _13, _14, _17, _20)

 

    obd_get_mod_rpc_slot+0x120/0x564 [obdclass]   <-- blocked waiting for a

                                                      close slot

    ptlrpc_get_mod_rpc_slot+0x38/0x60 [ptlrpc]

    mdc_close+0x21c/0xe64 [mdc]                   <-- synchronous MDS_CLOSE

    lmv_close+0x1a8/0x480 [lmv]

    ll_close_inode_openhandle+0x404/0xcc8 [lustre]

    ll_md_real_close+0xa4/0x280 [lustre]

    ll_clear_inode+0x1a0/0x7d8 [lustre]

    ll_delete_inode+0x70/0x260 [lustre]

    evict+0xdc/0x240                              <-- final iput: nothing held

                                                      the inode active

    iput_final / iput / dentry_unlink_inode / __dentry_kill / dentry_kill / dput

    d_prune_aliases+0x164/0x1c8

    ll_prune_aliases+0x224/0x540 [lustre]

    ll_lock_cancel_bits+0x250/0xcc8 [lustre]

    ll_md_blocking_ast+0x1c0/0x3f4 [lustre]       <-- LDLM_CB_CANCELING

    ldlm_cancel_callback+0x6c/0x334 [ptlrpc]

    ldlm_cli_cancel_local+0xf8/0x76c [ptlrpc]

    ldlm_cli_cancel_list_local+0x10c/0x43c [ptlrpc] <-- batch (LRU) cancel

                                                        branch

    ldlm_bl_thread_blwi.constprop.0+0x244/0x490 [ptlrpc]

    ldlm_bl_thread_main+0x4e4/0x6c0 [ptlrpc]

 

Two facts from this stack are worth calling out:

 

1. The trigger is a local LRU cancel, not a received AST.

   ldlm_cli_cancel_list_local() under ldlm_bl_thread_blwi() is only reachable on

   the batch branch (blwi->blwi_count != 0), which is produced solely by

   ldlm_bl_to_thread_list(), whose only caller is ldlm_cancel_lru() – driven by

   the periodic SLV/pool recalc and namespace resize. A received

   LDLM_BL_CALLBACK would take the other branch (ldlm_handle_bl_callback()),

   which appears in ZERO traces across the entire event. LDLM_CB_CANCELING in

   the stack is not evidence of a received AST: every final cancel funnels

   through ldlm_cancel_callback() -> l_blocking_ast(..., LDLM_CB_CANCELING)

   regardless of what triggered it.

 

2. The inode was idle, not in use. ldlm_cancel_lru() only walks ns_unused_list,

   so the lock had zero l_readers/l_writers. Reaching d_prune_aliases ->

   iput_final -> evict proves nothing held the inode active. The

   MDS_INODELOCK_OPEN bit was held for a CACHED open handle – Lustre keeps open

   state cached under the inode lock to avoid a re-open round-trip, and that

   cached och does not take an active DLM reference. So the lock was

   LRU-eligible precisely BECAUSE it was idle, and cancelling it is the client

   voluntarily returning cached open state.

 

The contended resource

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

 

A hung service thread dumped the resource, confirming the OPEN bit and the

resulting pile-up:

 

    Resource: [0x240000578:0x55a:0x0].0x0  ns: mdt-<fsname>-MDT-A_UUID

              refcount = 5

    Granted locks (in reverse order):

      lock: ...157d7741  mode: CR/CR  res:[0x240000578:0x55a:0x0]

            bits 0x5/0x0  nid: 0@lo  expref: 17273

    Waiting locks:

      lock: ...159cee6c  mode: --/CW  res:[0x240000578:0x55a:0x0]

            bits 0x2/0x0  nid: local

 

bits 0x5 = MDS_INODELOCK_LOOKUP | MDS_INODELOCK_OPEN; the granted lock is held

by MDT-A's own internal client (0@lo), and a waiting UPDATE (bits 0x2) writer is

queued behind it indefinitely.

 

The pool being dead is what caused the evictions

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

 

    lock callback timer expired after 102s, ldlm_bl_timeout 100s:

        evicting client at 0@lo

    <fsname>MDT-A-mdc...: Connection to <fsname>-MDT-A (at 0@lo) was lost

    lock timed out (enqueued 302s ago); not entering recovery in server code

        [repeats every 2-5 min]

    lock callback timer expired after 153s: evicting client at <client-nid>

        [regular clients follow]

 

expired_lock_main() only fires for a lock whose blocking AST was already SENT

(l_blast_sent), so these are ASTs going unanswered as a CONSEQUENCE of the

drained pool – MDT-A's server could not get its own client side to respond.

 

Why the import never recovered

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

 

MDT-A's MDC to MDT-B logged no "Connection restored" for the whole window. The

replays were being rejected:

 

    ptlrpc_replay_interpret() @@@ status 301 ... o101-><fsname>MDT-B-mdc...

 

o101 = LDLM_ENQUEUE, status 301 = ELDLM_LOCK_ABORTED. The peer MDTs had

in-flight cross-MDT lock enqueues at failover; during MDT-B's recovery those

enqueues were aborted, which aborted the whole replay set, so the MDC never

reached FULL and was disconnected as a stale client – marking the import

invalid. MDT-B's log confirms this from the other side (the peer joined

recovery, then "disconnect stale client", and recovery ended with 2 of 583

clients evicted). Only the two peer MDTs holding in-flight cross-MDT locks were

affected; the other 581 clients replayed cleanly.

 

The resulting close failures are visible as:

 

    ll_close_inode_openhandle() ... inode [0x240000578:0xa8:0x0]

        mdc close failed: rc = -108

 

-108 is -ESHUTDOWN, exactly what ptlrpc_import_delay_req() returns once the

import is invalid.

 

Ruled out

~~~~~~~~~

 

No OOM, page-allocation-failure, shrinker or reclaim activity anywhere in the

window (this is not memory pressure – the LRU cancel is volume-driven cache

trimming). No truncate_inode_pages / folio_wait / wait_on_page in any trace. No

received-blocking-AST frames.

 

 

3. ROOT CAUSE

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 

mdc_close() takes a modify-RPC slot and then waits synchronously:

 

    ptlrpc_get_mod_rpc_slot(req);

    rc = ptlrpc_queue_wait(req);

    ptlrpc_put_mod_rpc_slot(req);

 

A plain close has rq_send_state = LUSTRE_IMP_FULL and no rq_allow_replay, so on

a non-FULL import ptlrpc_import_delay_req() sets delay = 1 and the request

sleeps with no timeout – delayed requests carry rq_waiting, are skipped by both

ptlrpc_set_next_timeout() and ptlrpc_expired_set(), and are only ever woken by

ptlrpc_wake_delayed() when the import reaches FULL.

 

Meanwhile the slot it already holds is the ONLY close slot:

 

    /* A slot is available if

     * - number of modify RPCs in flight is less than the max

     * - it's a close RPC and no other close request is in flight */

    avail = cli->cl_mod_rpcs_in_flight < cli->cl_max_mod_rpcs_in_flight ||

            (close_req && cli->cl_close_rpcs_in_flight == 0);

 

so every later close finds avail == false and sleeps uninterruptibly in

wait_woken(..., MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT).

 

The defect is that obd_get_mod_rpc_slot() has no notion of import state. Threads

asleep on cl_mod_rpcs_waitq are woken only by modify-RPC completion, so when the

import is invalidated – which the status-301 recovery abort guarantees – the

waiters are waiting on an event that can never occur. Running this path from

ldlm_bl context turns that into a pool-wide, cluster-visible deadlock.

Here's how I reproduced and validated the fix using fail injection parameters

Parameter Value Effect
fail_loc 0x32e OBD_FAIL_LDLM_REPLAY_PAUSE — pauses inside ldlm_cancel_unused_locks_for_replay during reconnect
fail_val 2 2-second pause duration
The 2s pause widens the window where lock cancel callbacks (bl_ast) fire while the import is still in REPLAY_LOCKS state. This ensures enough bl threads enter mdc_close() simultaneously to drain the pool.

Prerequisites: 3-MDT filesystem, client at $DIR

1. Generate OPEN-bit locks

lctl set_param llite.*.opencache_threshold_count=1
lfs mkdir -c 3 $DIR/testdir
for i in $(seq 0 99); do echo data > $DIR/testdir/f$i; done
for i in $(seq 0 99); do cat $DIR/testdir/f$i > /dev/null; done

2. Verify locks on MDT0001

lctl get_param -n ldlm.namespaces.MDT0001mdc*.lock_count

Should show > 50

3. Arm fail_loc on client

lctl set_param fail_val=2 fail_loc=0x32e

4. Crash MDT0001 (force stop + restart the MDS instance)

5. Wait 90s, then check:

lctl get_param mdc.MDT0001.import | grep state:

With fix: FULL

Without fix: REPLAY_LOCKS (permanent deadlock)

6. Try new activity:

mkdir $DIR/newdir

With fix: succeeds instantly

Without fix: hangs forever (only reboot clears)

Root cause, with a one-line fix. Patch:
https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/67599

The reported stack is ten ldlm_bl threads blocked in obd_get_mod_rpc_slot().
They are acquirers, not the holder. For all ten to be parked, the avail test
in genops.c requires cl_close_rpcs_in_flight != 0, so an unseen thread held
the reserved close slot. That thread is the import's own ldlm_lock_replay
kthread, and it is absent from the report because ptlrpc_set_wait() sleeps
TASK_IDLE / TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE and is invisible to khungtaskd. The mechanism
predicts its own absence from the evidence.

At LUSTRE_IMP_REPLAY_LOCKS, __ldlm_replay_locks() first calls
ldlm_cancel_unused_locks_for_replay(), which runs every unused lock's
CANCELING AST inline on that thread. A LOOKUP/PERM cancel reaches
ll_prune_aliases(), drops the last dentry of an inode whose open handle is
still cached by an OPEN lock, and ll_clear_inode() then has to issue
MDS_CLOSE. That close is parked by ptlrpc_import_delay_req() while holding
the close slot, and the import cannot reach FULL until the same thread
returns and drops imp_replay_inflight.

The cycle is permanent, and that is provable from source: a non-FULL import
is not pinged (pinger.c), cannot be set DISCON (ptlrpc_set_import_discon()
requires FULL), cannot be advanced by the state machine (imp_replay_inflight
never reaches 0), and ptlrpc_abort_inflight() skips requests of the current
generation. No timeout, eviction or reconnect breaks it, which is consistent
with the duration observed and with the reboot-only resolution.

Note the page-cache theory in the original analysis does not hold: there is
no truncate_inode_pages or page-wait frame anywhere in the full stack.

Fix: set rq_allow_replay on the close so it is not deferred during its own
import's recovery. The target already processes MDS_CLOSE while recovering -
tgt_filter_recovery_request() lists it, and target_queue_recovery_request()
processes rather than queues a request with no transno, which a fresh close
has. Direct in-tree precedent: ldlm_cli_cancel_req() does exactly this for a
cross-MDT LDLM_CANCEL, for the same deadlock class, but is gated on
OBD_CONNECT_MDS_MDS so it never covers a close issued through llite.

Measured with a matched A/B, same harness, this one line as the only
variable:

unpatched patched
o35 "req waiting for recovery" 1 0
o35 "allow during recovery" 0 26
ldlm_bl parked (state S) 727 samples 0 of 730
imp_replay_inflight stuck at 10 drained to 0
recovery outcome COMPLETE COMPLETE

Also built and smoke-tested on 2.15.8 (kernel 5.10) against a live 3-MDT DNE
filesystem: all MDCs and OSCs reach FULL, with normal I/O timings.
recovery-small tests 1, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and the new 171 all pass on the patched
build.

On the two options discussed earlier: option A is this fix. Option C appears
to be a no-op - mdc_cancel_weight() already returns 0 for any lock holding
MDS_INODELOCK_OPEN, and the replay pass is exactly the no-wait policy that
consults it; separately, the observed close came from a LOOKUP/PERM cancel,
so protecting OPEN-bit locks would not have prevented it. Worth noting that
ldlm_cancel_no_wait_policy()'s own comment promises not to pick locks that
would need an RPC "to close a file" - that contract is already violated
today, and mdc_cancel_weight() cannot honour it.

The open-locking hypothesis is correct and load-bearing: ll_md_close() skips
the real close precisely when md_lock_match() finds a cached OPEN lock, which
is what leaves the handle for eviction to close. Without opencache the path
is not reachable from an AST at all.

Why there is no reproducer. A test that fails without the fix would have to
observe that the close was parked on imp_delayed_list, and that is not
observable through any stable interface - mdc.*.import exposes rpcs:

{ inflight, unregistering, timeouts, avg_waittime }

and no delayed-request
counter. The only remaining signal is the CDEBUG text from
ptlrpc_import_delay_req(), and those two strings are the two branches of the
very "if" that rq_allow_replay controls, so a test grepping them asserts only
that the flag just set is set. It restates the implementation, cannot catch a
bug in it, and stops asserting anything the moment the message is reworded.
The patch therefore carries a regression guard only: recovery-small test_171
passes with and without the fix, and checks recovery COMPLETE, zero
evictions, and every seeded file still at its original size with a matching
checksum. The size matters because mdc_close() carries an mdt_rec_setattr, so
a lost close shows up as a short file.

What is not established. The original field condition is not reproduced.
Every lab variant either self-heals once the target returns or requires the
target never to return, and the defining feature - persisting for over two
hours after the peer was healthy again - was not reproduced. The import state
was never captured in the field, so identifying it as REPLAY_LOCKS is
inference from the timeline. On a single-client, single-node configuration
there is no replay window to drive a close into at all: the import reports
"FULL state after 0 sec" and not one RPC of any opcode is delayed. This fix
also removes only the demonstrated trigger, not the whole class - the untimed
wait in obd_get_mod_rpc_slot() and the inline Data-on-MDT flush in
ll_lock_cancel_bits() are untouched and remain separate blocking points.

Update: root cause of the reported stack, and a fix that has been tested against it.

The hung ldlm_bl threads in the report are doing ordinary LRU cancellation.
The close comes from evicting the PARENT directory of a pruned dentry:
d_prune_aliases() drops the dentry's reference on its parent, and if that was
the parent's last reference the parent is evicted and ll_clear_inode() closes
its cached open handle synchronously. If that handle's MDT is down, the
ldlm_bl thread waits for as long as the MDT is away. The pool is shared by
every namespace on the node, so cancellation for healthy MDTs stops too. With
DNE the lock and the open handle can be on different MDTs.

Reproduced on mainline, matching the reported stack frame for frame. One lab
assist: the parent must be evicted on its last iput, forced here with
llite.*.inode_cache=0.

The earlier theory that the replay thread issues the close is wrong for these
trees: the pre-replay cancel uses the no-wait policy and mdc_cancel_weight()
refuses OPEN locks.

Fix posted as https://review.whamcloud.com/67599 patchset 17 (llite only):
closes and eviction iputs from the cancel path run in a per-sb workqueue; the
cancelling thread keeps the old ordering while the MDT is reachable and stops
waiting once it is not. Two new recovery-small tests, test_172 and test_173,
fail without the fix and pass with it. Full recovery-small passes except
test_156 (tot_granted after OST eviction), which fails the same way unpatched
on this setup.
